# Gloton Rust CLI and Clap contract

## Package and toolchain

`Cargo.toml` owns package metadata, the edition, minimum Rust version, unsafe-code policy, dependencies, and publication state. `rust-toolchain.toml` is the only compiler/component selector. `Cargo.lock` stays committed because Gloton is an executable.

A dependency or feature needs a current code consumer and a testable failure contract. Do not add an async runtime, provider SDK, persistence layer, observability stack, FFI, benchmark harness, profiler, or workspace before implemented behavior requires it.

## Command boundary

Clap derive owns the process grammar. Help text, stdout, stderr, and exit status are public behavior. A product command is present only when its effect and failure semantics are implemented; planned repository discovery or synchronization must not appear as working CLI behavior.

## Task and verification boundary

Normal repository work goes through one of the eleven public Just recipes. Local and hosted completion use `just ci`. For CLI contract changes, test the compiled process and distinguish success, usage failure, and unknown input by status and output stream. For policy changes, `tests/harness.rs` must distinguish canonical bytes from stale, missing, extra, or hand-edited generated carriers.

## Negative space

Do not add a second command parser, task runner, hook framework, release path, provider abstraction, or fallback interface for hypothetical consumers. Do not suppress compiler or Clippy failures; fix the source or change the owning policy with evidence.
